name: Booker T. Washington
role: Educator, author and president of Tuskegee Institute (1856-1915)
summary: Washington led Tuskegee Institute and was the dominant Black leader of his time, urging industry, property, thrift and education as the base for Black advancement while publicly accepting social separation and a gradual path. He favoured honest, equally applied education or property tests for the vote, rejected revolution and socialism, opposed emigration to Africa, and privately funded court challenges to disfranchisement and segregation.
